passages.context: Sections 2 and 8 were read in the complete exposition with adjacent sections in view. Section 2 construes judgment proceeding from God's countenance and the eyes as eyes of the heart; section 8 reads the eye's pupil through Christ's humanity and the wings as divine love and mercy.

passages.context: Sections 1-11 and 15-22 were read as one bounded exposition. The lifted soul rises from carnal longing, trust abandons self-reliance, waiting depends on mercy, enemies include inward and ecclesial dangers, and the closing petition expands to the redemption of Israel.
passages.notes: The English page is headed Psalm 25 while its verse links and Augustine locus use Vulgate Psalm 24. Augustine's ecclesial applications are received exegesis and do not identify the psalm's original enemies.

passages.context: Sections 21-23 were read with the psalm's closing movement in view. Section 21 distinguishes former animal figures from the one saving sacrifice and the contrite-heart offering; section 22 identifies David as a figure of the Church; section 23 directly treats accepted sacrifices, praise, and whole-person holocaust.
passages.notes: The English page is headed Psalm 51 while its verse links and Augustine locus use Vulgate Psalm 50. Section 23, not section 21, is the direct exposition of the source verse used by the Communion.

passages.context: Sections 16-19 and 23-24 were read in the complete exposition. Augustine makes the cry the prayer of Christ's body, reads evening-morning-noon as continual Christological prayer, treats peace amid nearby division, and at section 23 directly exhorts the little one to cast care upon the nourishing Lord; section 24 begins the following judgment verse.

passages.context: Sections 3-5 were read with sections 1-2 as adjacent setup. Augustine reads Zion and Jerusalem as the heavenly homeland already held by hope, the vow as completed in the resurrection of the whole person, and every flesh as people of every condition and nation coming through Christ's assumed flesh.
